results.title: Microsoft hasn't had a coherent GUI strategy since Petzold
results.text: I was recently exploring "an OS from scratch" architecture with ChatGPT. Apart from the central idea that I wanted it to be a capability OS, I also started thinking about how I'd make GUI apps and what layers would naturally make sense. The cleanest design I came up with works like this: 1. At Layer_1 OS provides panes or windows to which apps can render whatever graphics using OS gpu lib (think Raylib, but maybe a bit simpler). results.text: Regarding graphics, CBQN is not very suited to doing these natively as it runs on the CPU rather than GPU and has only double-precision and not single-precision floats. So, can you do some simple animation at 60FPS? Probably. Can you make a competitive game engine with it? Definitely not.
